title: Reflection Lexicon — Further Linguistic Analysis
content_html:
Reflection Lexicon — Further Linguistic Analysis

Concrete directions for deeper analysis.

1. Lexical semantics

  • Map semantic fields (optics, perception, memory, meta) and tighten group labels.
  • Build a network of lexical relations: synonymy/antonymy (e.g., clarity ↔ opacity), hypernyms (e.g., memory ⊃ episodic/semantic).
  • Polysemy inventory: e.g., reflection = optical image vs. introspection; classify senses and attach examples.

2. Cross-lingual alignment (EN ↔ Cantonese)

  • Translation strategies: direct vs. idiomatic vs. technical terms (e.g., 記憶術).
  • Literal–idiomatic divergence: use your “literal gloss” column to quantify distance from word-for-word mapping.
  • Part-of-speech alignment: English nouns vs. Cantonese noun/verb/adjective realizations.

3. Morphology (Cantonese / Chinese)

  • Compound patterns: prefixes/suffixes and morphemes (e.g., 記/憶, 再-, 自我-, -術). Count and visualize templates X‑記憶, 自我‑…
  • Character productivity: which characters function as productive morphemes (e.g., 記, 憶, 光, 影, 證)?
  • Affix-like behaviour: quantify pseudo-affixes (e.g., -術) and semantic roles.

4. Phonology & phonotactics (Cantonese)

  • Tone distribution (done in the report): which tones dominate? Are memory-cluster terms skewed to certain tones?
  • Syllable structure: counts (done), coda distribution (-n/-ng/-p/-t/-k/Ø), onsets (z/c/j…).
  • Homophony: cluster by identical Jyutping strings; check where homophones map to different meanings.

5. Orthography & character semantics

  • Radicals and semantic hints: group by radicals (e.g., 言/心/光/見) and correlate with semantic fields.
  • Character frequency (done): extend to bigram/trigram frequencies at the character level.

6. Discourse & frame semantics

  • Align each word to frames: Seeing → Attending → Remembering → Retrieving → Evaluating → Meta.
  • Build a script (event sequence) and test alternative orderings; compute path coherence (e.g., minimal cross-frame jumps).

7. Conceptual metaphor & image schemas

  • Tag metaphor mappings (e.g., SEEING→KNOWING, KNOWLEDGE→CLARITY) and count instantiations.
  • Use the Source–Path–Goal schema to justify the overall progression.

8. Usage-based / corpus methods (optional expansion)

  • Collocation profiles: for each English item, extract top collocates; compare with Chinese collocates for the translation.
  • Distributional semantics: embed the English list with word vectors, cluster, and compare to a character- or word-level embedding of the Chinese items.

9. Psycholinguistic features

  • Concreteness/AoA ratings for English; test whether “optics” terms are more concrete than “meta” terms.
  • Valence/arousal: map affective norms (e.g., nostalgia vs. evidence).
  • Memory architecture mapping: align encoding→storage→retrieval terms to standard models; check completeness.

10. Assessment design / pedagogy

  • Build minimal pairs (clarity–opacity; reflection–refraction).
  • Create spaced-repetition decks using your phases as interleaved strands.
  • Add romanization practice: tone‑pair drills for items with similar segments across tones.
